comparison: Use the maximum of the two sample-size parameters, coerced to the reals, in both logarithms, and multiply by the same user-specified positive c-xi. The source specifies ln(max(N,T))*ln(ln(max(N,T))); replacing max by the product NT would use the separate simulation alternative, not this definition. Real.log is total with a zero and negative-input extension, so its mere evaluability does not justify the ordinary double-log expression at max(N,T)=1 or positivity of the threshold at every small size. The asymptotic sample-size domain must supply the intended logarithm and eventual positivity conditions; c-xi positive alone does not do that.
gap: Maximum and real logarithm directly express the threshold on its intended sample-size domain, with small-size logarithm conditions retained explicitly.
searches: Inspect Real.log 38-45 and max_le_iff against the prescribed maximum-based double logarithm
The arithmetic is available, but Real.log's total extension must not silently define excluded ordinary-log inputs or justify positive thresholds at all sizes.

comparison: Condition on the sigma-algebra generated only by the true-support coordinates x_S*, require conditional mean beta*_S* dot x_S* and conditional variance at most sigma squared almost everywhere under the given law, and impose the marginal second-moment bounds for every coordinate. Retain support(beta*)=S* and sigma squared positive. The real conditional expectation and variance operations have fallback values outside their integrability and sub-sigma-algebra conditions, so those conditions must accompany the statistical interpretation; marginal second moments give square integrability of the finite linear mean, while the finite conditional variance is interpreted in its genuine probabilistic sense. Do not condition on all coordinates instead, impose homoscedastic equality, infer residual independence, or turn this conditional-mean model into an SCM or a causal exogeneity assumption.
gap: Conditional expectation and variance provide the required operations, with the true-support conditioning algebra, almost-everywhere constraints and moment conditions specified separately.
searches: Inspect condExp, CondVar.lean 30-40 and MemLp against the distribution class in (2.1)
The library supports conditional centering and squared residuals; preserving the smaller conditioning sigma-algebra and ruling out fallback-zero interpretations are essential.

comparison: Index observations by environment and one common sample index set of cardinality n. Within each environment the pair-valued observations have the same specified law mu^(e) and are independent, and the data blocks from different environments are independent as the source explicitly requires. The full array may therefore be modeled by an independent family, but identical distribution is asserted only within each environment: the laws can differ across environments while sharing membership in U_(beta*,sigma squared). Uniform weight is the real reciprocal of the nonempty finite environment count. Preserve balanced n and equal weights; do not import the appendix's unequal-size/weight generalization or weaken across-environment independence to uncorrelatedness.
gap: Independence and identical-distribution predicates express the sampling design once the environment-specific laws, balanced sizes and uniform weights are supplied.
searches: Inspect iIndepFun and IdentDistrib against the within- and across-environment clauses
The family predicate can encode joint independence while equality of pushforward laws remains restricted to observations from the same environment.

comparison: For each fixed output coordinate u_j, take the L2 seminorm of the kernel section in its input coordinate u_k over [0,1], then the pointwise supremum over all u_j in [0,1]. Form the row sum or finite row maximum of these block quantities as separately defined. An essential supremum over the outer coordinate is not the stated supremum, and an induced operator norm, Hilbert-Schmidt norm or Frobenius norm need not equal this mixed kernel quantity. This depends on supplied kernel representatives, which can matter at exceptional outer points even if an integral operator is unchanged almost everywhere. Preserve section measurability, finiteness and boundedness when using real norms/suprema; extended L2 norms avoid treating divergent integrals as real zero. A nonempty block index set is needed for Finset.max'. The motivating estimated Theta row is not an extra input or assumption of the generic Xi construction.
gap: L2 seminorms, supremum and finite row operations express the mixed kernel quantities; they require representative and finiteness conditions and are not the induced operator norm.
searches: Inspect eLpNorm, lpNorm, csSup_le_iff and Finset.max' against (3.5)
The inner L2 operation and outer supremum are available separately; lpNorm's real fallback and essential-supremum interpretation would otherwise change the source quantity.

comparison: Use a matrix with p coordinate rows and m machine columns, each entry restricted to the three labels negative, positive and null. A three-element type or a real-valued matrix with membership in {-1,0,1} represents the input exactly. Real.sign produces those values when local real scores are supplied, including zero mapped to zero, but the generic sign-matrix definition does not require any particular score estimator or thresholding rule. Keep rows and columns in the source order, so each vote aggregates a row across machines. No binary tie convention, independence of entries, differential privacy or majority-vote correctness follows merely from being such a matrix; those belong to the separate mechanisms and assumptions.
gap: Finite matrices and the ternary sign function supply the representation, with local estimation and voting mechanisms remaining separate.
searches: Inspect Matrix at Defs.lean 54-58 and Real.sign at Basic/Real/Sign.lean 31-35
The matrix indexing and three sign values match, including the null value; the representation does not prescribe a local estimator or private voting rule.
